clinician.final_diagnosis: necrotizing fasciitis of the perineum from a multidrug-resistant bacteria, the carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 52-year-old woman with AML developed fever and vulvar inflammatory signs including pain, swelling, pruritus, and hard phlegm on day +11 post-chemotherapy. Blood and vulvar exudate cultures isolated carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae resistant to meropenem and amikacin but sensitive to tigecycline and colistin. Pelvic CT on day +12 showed no abscess or gas collections. The patient underwent superficial debridement of soft tissue above fascia in the perineal area, followed by ICU admission due to transient multiorgan dysfunction. Despite initial broad-spectrum antibiotics including vancomycin, meropenem, amikacin, and colistin, cellulitis recurred at surgical borders prompting antibiotic rotation. This clinical, microbiological, imaging, and surgical course supports the diagnosis of necrotizing fasciitis caused by carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella.
